items.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025
items.q: a few that I’ve played for my whole life, the number 4 [scats] that one. I transposed it into all twelve keys.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well the fact that you recognized the changes that Schubert was using I think is significant anyway.

Oh yeah. I mean I just had an innate sense of harmony. But you know everyone is born with certain abilities and then it’s just a matter of okay, if you’re going to try to get in the pond with the big boys, all right, it’s great that you can do this and you can do that, but can you play “All the Things You Are” in all twelve keys? In any tempo? I mean I know Bird kicked George Shearing’s ass one night. I heard that story. You know George Shearing came over from England and he’s sitting there at some club on 52nd…

a few that I’ve played for my whole life, the number 4 [scats] that one. I transposed it into all twelve keys. And I do it with my eyes closed and you know, all that kind of stuff. Because there’s no cheating in music. I mean either you can or you can’t do it. And then I have to slow down. Okay I know what it sounds like but my fingering sucks when I’m playing it in F sharp minor. I’m like, “What’s the right fingering here?”
